documents.title: Reset a forgotten password
documents.content: To reset a forgotten password, open the self-service password portal, choose Forgot password, and verify with the registered mobile number or authenticator app. The new password must be at least 14 characters. If self-service is not registered, the service desk can reset it after identity verification with two security questions.

documents.title: Service desk support hours
documents.content: The service desk answers calls Monday to Friday from 7 AM to 7 PM Central time. Priority 1 outages are handled 24 hours a day, 7 days a week through the on-call line. Requests submitted outside business hours are picked up the next business morning.

documents.title: Request a new laptop
documents.content: New laptop requests need manager approval and are fulfilled within five business days. Standard models are listed in the hardware catalog; non-standard models need an exception from the hardware review board. Return the old device within ten days of receiving the replacement.

documents.title: Connect to the VPN
documents.content: Install the approved VPN client from the software center, sign in with your work account, and approve the multifactor prompt. If the client reports a certificate error, restart the device on the office network or run the device compliance check, then try again.

documents.title: Escalate an urgent issue
documents.content: Urgent issues that stop a whole team from working are Priority 1. Say that it is urgent and the assistant will transfer the call to a human agent, who opens a Priority 1 ticket and pages the on-call engineer. Target response for Priority 1 is 15 minutes.

documents.title: Unlock a locked account
documents.content: Accounts lock for 30 minutes after ten failed sign-in attempts. Wait 30 minutes or use the self-service portal and choose Unlock my account, then verify with your authenticator app. Repeated lockouts usually come from an old credential saved on a phone or a mapped drive; remove it to stop further lockouts.

documents.title: Password expiry and rotation rules
documents.content: Work passwords expire every 180 days. You get email reminders 14, 7, and 1 day before expiry. A new password cannot match any of your last 12. Service accounts follow a separate 90-day rotation managed by the identity team.

documents.title: Set up multifactor authentication
documents.content: Multifactor authentication is required for every account. Install the authenticator app on your phone, open the security info page, choose Add sign-in method, and scan the QR code. Add a second method such as a phone number as a backup in case you replace your phone.

documents.title: Replaced or lost phone with the authenticator app
documents.content: If you replaced or lost the phone that holds your authenticator app, call the service desk. After identity verification the agent issues a temporary access pass valid for eight hours, which you use to register the app on the new phone. Report a lost phone as a security incident as well.

documents.title: New employee account activation
documents.content: New employee accounts are created three business days before the start date. The manager receives a temporary access pass to share on day one. The new employee signs in, sets a password, and registers multifactor authentication within the first 24 hours.

documents.title: Guest Wi-Fi for visitors
documents.content: Visitors use the guest Wi-Fi network. Reception issues a daily access code that is valid for 24 hours. The guest network has internet access only and cannot reach internal systems. Employees should always use the corporate Wi-Fi with their work account.

documents.title: Slow VPN or dropped connection
documents.content: If the VPN is slow or drops, first test your home internet speed; at least 10 megabits per second is recommended for calls. Switch to a wired connection if possible, close large downloads, and reconnect to the nearest gateway. If drops continue for more than a day, open a ticket with the time of each drop.

documents.title: Remote desktop to an office computer
documents.content: Remote desktop to an office computer works only over the VPN. The office computer must stay powered on and be registered for remote access by the service desk. Request remote access through the self-service portal under Network requests; approval takes one business day.

documents.title: Laptop will not turn on
documents.content: Connect the original charger for 15 minutes, then hold the power button for 20 seconds and release. If the charging light does not come on, try another outlet. If the laptop still does not start, request a loaner device at the service desk walk-up counter so you can keep working while it is repaired.

documents.title: Loaner devices
documents.content: Loaner laptops are available at the walk-up counter for up to 14 days while your device is repaired. Bring your badge. Loaners come with standard software only, so save work to your cloud drive and not to the loaner itself. Return the loaner within two days of getting your repaired device back.

documents.title: Mobile phone enrollment
documents.content: To read work email on a personal phone, install the company portal app and enroll the phone. Enrollment protects work data only and does not let the company see personal photos or messages. Work data can be removed remotely if the phone is lost, without erasing personal content.

documents.title: Printer is offline or jammed
documents.content: For a jammed printer, open the front panel and remove paper slowly in the direction of the arrows. If the printer shows offline, check the network cable and restart it. Office printers are listed in the print portal by floor; pick another printer on the same floor while you wait for facilities.

documents.title: Device refresh cycle
documents.content: Laptops are refreshed every four years and phones every three years. You receive an email about 30 days before your refresh date with a link to pick a standard model. Devices can be refreshed early only for a verified hardware failure or a documented job requirement.

documents.title: Install approved software
documents.content: Approved software installs from the software center without admin rights. Search for the app name and choose Install. If an app is not in the software center, request it through the self-service portal; new software needs a security review, which takes about five business days.

documents.title: Request a software license
documents.content: Paid software licenses need manager approval and a cost center. Request the license in the self-service portal under Software requests. Standard licenses are assigned within one business day of approval. Unused licenses are reclaimed after 60 days without sign-in.

documents.title: Application keeps crashing
documents.content: If an application keeps crashing, restart the device first, then check for updates in the software center. Repair the app from the software center with the Repair option. If it still crashes, open a ticket with the app name, the time of the crash, and a screenshot of any error message.

documents.title: Update schedule for devices
documents.content: Security updates install automatically on the second Tuesday of each month. Devices restart outside working hours if they are on and plugged in. You can postpone a restart for up to 72 hours; after that the device restarts automatically to stay compliant.

documents.title: Shared mailbox access
documents.content: Access to a shared mailbox is requested by the mailbox owner or your manager in the self-service portal. Access appears in your mail app within two hours of approval. If it does not appear, restart the mail app. Shared mailboxes do not need their own password.

documents.title: Mailbox is full
documents.content: Mailboxes hold 100 gigabytes. When you reach 95 percent, archive older mail to the online archive, which is unlimited, and empty the deleted items folder. Large attachments are best shared as cloud links instead of files.

documents.title: Report a suspicious email
documents.content: If an email looks suspicious, do not click links or open attachments. Use the Report phishing button in your mail app, which sends it to the security team and removes it from your inbox. If you already clicked a link or entered your password, call the service desk right away and say it is a security incident.

documents.title: Set an out-of-office reply
documents.content: Set an automatic reply in your mail app under Settings, Automatic replies. Add separate messages for internal and external senders and set a start and end time. Automatic replies can also be set from the web version of mail when you are away from your laptop.

documents.title: Meeting room audio and video problems
documents.content: If a meeting room has no audio or video, check that the room console shows the meeting, then press the room reset button on the console. Make sure the laptop is not also joined with audio, which causes echo. For urgent room problems during a meeting, call the facilities line shown on the console.

documents.title: Report a lost or stolen device
documents.content: Report a lost or stolen laptop or phone to the service desk immediately, day or night. The device is locked and work data is wiped remotely. Also file a report with building security if it was lost on site. A replacement is issued after the report is filed.

documents.title: Data classification basics
documents.content: Data is classified as Public, Internal, Confidential, or Restricted. Confidential and Restricted files must carry a sensitivity label, are encrypted automatically, and must not be shared with personal email addresses. When unsure, label a document Confidential and ask the data owner.

documents.title: Using USB storage devices
documents.content: USB storage is blocked by default on work laptops. Use cloud sharing instead. If a job requires USB storage, request an exception in the self-service portal; approved exceptions allow only encrypted company-issued drives and expire after 90 days.

documents.title: Check the status of a request
documents.content: Every request has a number that starts with SR, such as SR-1001. Say or enter the number and the assistant reads back the current status, owning team, and last update. You can also see all of your requests in the self-service portal under My requests.

documents.title: Priority levels and response targets
documents.content: Priority 1 means a whole team or critical system is down, with a 15 minute response target. Priority 2 means one person cannot work, with a 4 hour target. Priority 3 is a problem with a workaround, answered within one business day. Priority 4 is a question or request, answered within three business days.

documents.title: Talk to a human agent
documents.content: Ask for a human agent at any time and the call is transferred to the service desk queue. Current wait time is announced before transfer. If all agents are busy, you can leave a callback number and the next available agent calls you back in the same business day.

documents.title: Planned maintenance and outage notices
documents.content: Planned maintenance happens on Saturdays between 10 PM and 2 AM Central time and is announced on the status page at least five days ahead. During an unplanned outage the status page is updated every 30 minutes. Check the status page before calling about a widespread problem.

documents.title: Give feedback on a resolved request
documents.content: When a request is resolved you receive a short survey by email. Feedback goes to the team that handled the request and to service desk leadership. If a request was closed but the problem is not fixed, reply to the resolution email within seven days to reopen it.

documents.title: Working remotely from another country
documents.content: Working from another country for more than ten business days needs approval from your manager and the security team at least two weeks before travel. Some countries are restricted and devices cannot connect from them. Request approval in the self-service portal under Travel requests.

documents.title: Acceptable use of work devices
documents.content: Work devices are for business use, with limited personal use allowed if it does not affect work or security. Do not install unapproved software, disable security tools, or store personal media libraries on work devices. Report any accidental policy breach to the service desk.

documents.title: Employee departure and device return
documents.content: When an employee leaves, the manager submits a departure request at least five business days before the last day. Access ends at the close of the last working day. Laptops, phones, and badges are returned to the walk-up counter or with a prepaid shipping label for remote staff.

documents.title: Badge not working
documents.content: If your badge does not open a door, hold it flat against the reader for two seconds. Badges deactivate after 30 days without use and when a password is reset after a security incident. Reception can reactivate a badge after checking your identity, or issue a temporary badge for the day.

documents.title: Book a desk or meeting room
documents.content: Desks and meeting rooms are booked in the workplace app up to 14 days ahead. Check in within 15 minutes of the start time or the booking is released. Rooms for more than 12 people need approval from facilities and are best booked at least three days ahead.
